user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure tools are installed: `git`, `git-svn`, `svn`
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

---

## Phase 1 — Preparation (8:00–9:00 AM)

### 1.1 Audit the SVN Repo
```bash
# Check repo size and history depth
svn info https://your-svn-repo/url
svn log https://your-svn-repo/url | grep "^r" | wc -l
```

### 1.2 Build an Authors File
SVN uses usernames; Git needs `Name <email>` format.

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors
svn log https://your-svn-repo/url -q \
  | grep "^r" \
  | awk -F'|' '{print $2}' \
  | sort -u \
  | sed 's/ //g' > authors.txt
```

Edit `authors.txt` into this format:
```
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
```

### 1.3 Identify Repo Layout
```
Standard layout?   /trunk  /branches  /tags
Non-standard?      Custom folder structure
```

---

## Phase 2 — Clone SVN → Git (9:00–11:00 AM)

### Standard Layout
```bash
git svn clone https://your-svn-repo/url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors.txt \
  my-project-git
```

### Non-Standard Layout
```bash
git svn clone https://your-svn-repo/url \
  --trunk=trunk \
  --branches=branches \
  --tags=tags \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  my-project-git
```

> ⏱️ **Time varies** — small repos finish in minutes; large histories may take longer.

---

## Phase 3 — Clean Up the Git Repo (11:00 AM–1:00 PM)

```bash
cd my-project-git
```

### 3.1 Convert SVN Branches & Tags
```bash
# Convert remote SVN branches to local Git branches
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v "tags/" | grep -v trunk); do
  git branch "${branch##*/}" "$branch"
done

# Convert SVN tags to proper Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/"); do
  git tag "${tag##*/tags/}" "$tag"
  git branch -d -r "$tag"
done
```

### 3.2 Remove SVN Tracking References
```bash
git config --remove-section svn-remote.svn
rm -rf .git/svn
```

### 3.3 Clean Up `.gitignore`
```bash
# SVN uses svn:ignore — check if .gitignore was created
cat .gitignore

# Add common entries if missing
echo ".svn/" >> .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: clean up .gitignore post-migration"
```

### 3.4 Verify History
```bash
git log --oneline | head -20
git branch -a
git tag
```

---

## Phase 4 — Push to Remote Git Host (1:00–2:00 PM)

```bash
# Add your new remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/your-org/my-project-git.git

# Push main branch
git push -u origin main   # or master

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags
```

---

## Phase 5 — Validation (2:00–3:30 PM)

| Check | Command |
|---|---|
| Commit count matches | `git log --oneline \| wc -l` |
| All branches present | `git branch -a` |
| All tags present | `git tag -l` |
| Latest files correct | `git show HEAD` |
| Authors mapped correctly | `git log --format="%an %ae" \| sort -u` |

```bash
# Spot-check a specific SVN revision vs Git commit
svn log -r 42 https://your-svn-repo/url
git log --grep="r42"   # if --no-metadata was NOT used
```

---

## Phase 6 — Team Onboarding (3:30–5:00 PM)

### Each Developer Runs:
```bash
# Clone the new repo
git clone https://github.com/your-org/my-project-git.git

# Set identity if not global
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@company.com"
```

### Share a Quick-Reference Cheat Sheet

| SVN Command | Git Equivalent |
|---|---|
| `svn checkout` | `git clone` |
| `svn update` | `git pull` |
| `svn commit` | `git add` + `git commit` + `git push` |
| `svn revert` | `git checkout --` or `git restore` |
| `svn log` | `git log` |
| `svn diff` | `git diff` |
| `svn branch` | `git checkout -b` |

---

## End-of-Day Wrap-Up

- [ ] **Disable SVN repo** (set to read-only or archive it)
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines to point to Git
- [ ] Update any documentation or wikis with new repo URL
- [ ] Send team confirmation that migration is complete
- [ ] Keep SVN backup for **30 days** minimum before deleting

---

## Risk & Rollback

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Authors file incomplete | Migration fails loudly — fix and re-run |
| Large binary files | Consider Git LFS before pushing |
| SVN externals | Must be manually converted to Git submodules |
| CI/CD breaks | Keep SVN read-only until pipelines are verified |

> **Rollback:** SVN repo remains untouched until you explicitly archive it — safe to revert if needed.

Based on the migration plan, the top 3 risks are:

---

### 1. 🗂️ Incomplete Authors File
**Why it matters:** `git svn clone` will **abort entirely** if it encounters an SVN username not mapped in `authors.txt`, forcing you to restart the clone from scratch.

**Mitigation:** Double-check the extracted authors list before starting Phase 2, and add a catch-all fallback:
```bash
--authors-prog=fallback-author.sh
```

---

### 2. ⚙️ CI/CD Pipeline Breakage
**Why it matters:** Pipelines hardcoded to SVN paths, revision numbers, or checkout commands will **fail immediately** after cutover, potentially blocking deployments or releases.

**Mitigation:** Audit and update all pipeline configs **before** flipping the switch, and test in a staging pipeline first.

---

### 3. 📦 SVN Externals Not Migrating
**Why it matters:** `git svn` **silently ignores** SVN externals — they won't appear as Git submodules automatically, meaning dependencies or shared code could simply **go missing** without an obvious error.

**Mitigation:** Audit externals beforehand with:
```bash
svn propget svn:externals -R https://your-svn-repo/url
```
Then manually convert each to a Git submodule or vendored dependency.

---

> **Bottom line:** Authors and externals can derail the migration itself; CI/CD breakage is the most likely **post-migration** disruption.

## Pre-Migration Risk Checklist

- [ ] Extract and verify **all SVN authors** are mapped in `authors.txt` before cloning
- [ ] Audit **SVN externals** and plan manual conversion to submodules
- [ ] Update and test **CI/CD pipelines** against the new Git repo before cutover
Keep the SVN repository **read-only but intact** until the Git migration is fully verified — if anything goes wrong, re-enable write access and have developers revert to SVN.
Git must be installed on the machine performing the migration.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text: Run `git log --oneline | wc -l` and confirm the commit count matches the SVN revision count.
**8AM** Prep → **9AM** Clone → **11AM** Clean up → **1PM** Push → **2PM** Validate → **3:30PM** Onboard → **5PM** Done.

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
1. **`git-svn`** — clones SVN history into a Git repository
2. **`svn`** — audits the source repository before and during migration

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text: The **project or team lead** should approve the final cutover, confirming that validation checks have passed and all stakeholders have been notified.
Send a single team-wide message with a clear **cutover time, the new repo URL, and a freeze on SVN commits** before migration begins.

## Migration Recap

| Step | Key Action |
|---|---|
| **Prep** | Map authors, audit externals, freeze SVN |
| **Clone** | Use `git svn clone` with authors file |
| **Clean Up** | Convert branches/tags, fix `.gitignore` |
| **Push** | Push all branches and tags to remote |
| **Validate** | Confirm commit count and history |
| **Onboard** | Share new repo URL and Git cheat sheet |
| **Cutover** | Team lead approves, SVN set to read-only |

> **One day, one migration — back up first, validate before cutover, and keep SVN intact for 30 days.**

- Back up SVN first
- Freeze commits before starting
- Map all authors or clone will fail
- Check for SVN externals manually
- Clone with `git svn clone`
- Clean up branches and tags
- Push all branches and tags to remote
- Validate commit count
- Update CI/CD pipelines
- Team lead approves cutover
- Keep SVN read-only for 30 days
